what: Renowned feminist artist and film-maker Valie Export dies aged 85

clean_source_blocks.text: Export’s performances scandalised Austria in the 1960s, but are now recognised for exposing the objectification of the female body Valie Export, the Austrian performance artist and film-maker who inverted the male gaze in ways that were provocative, shocking and often outrageously fun, has died aged 85. The artist’s own foundation announced on Thursday evening that Export died in Vienna earlier the same day, three days before her 86th birthday. Continue reading...

Export’s performances scandalised Austria in the 1960s, but are now recognised for exposing the objectification of the female body Valie Export, the Austrian performance artist and film-maker who inverted the male gaze in ways that were provocative, shocking and often outrageously fun, has died aged 85. The artist’s own foundation announced on Thursday evening that Export died in Vienna earlier the same day, three days before her 86th birthday. She is best known for low-budget performances that scandalised Austria and Germany in the late 1960s, but have since been recognised as milestones in feminist art for exposing the objectification of the female body.

Valie Export, an influential figure in avant-garde feminist art, has died at the age of 85 in Vienna. The Austrian artist, born Waltraud Lehner in Linz in 1940, was a pioneering force in performance art. Export, who adopted her evocative pseudonym in the 1960s, challenged societal norms by appearing partially nude in public spaces early in her career. Her foundation highlighted that the capitalization of her name was an act of empowerment. Export's groundbreaking works include the performance art 'Tapp- und Tastkino' and 'Aktionshose: Genitalpanik,' along with experimental films like 'Unsichtbare Gegner' and 'Syntagma.' She significantly impacted the conceptual art scene with her provocative approach to addressing attitudes towards the female body and women's role in society.

“Valie was one of the most visionary feminist artists to emerge in Europe in the second half of the 20th century,” her gallerist Thaddaeus Ropac said in a statement. “Her passing marks the loss of a singular perspective in contemporary art, one that influenced artists across generations. Her pioneering work continues to be of such great urgency.” Born Waltraud Lehner in 1940 in Linz, Export boarded at a convent school as a child but left at 14 to study at the city’s School of Arts and Crafts. She married and had a child before she turned 20, but soon after decided to divorce and place her daughter into temporary care with an older sister in order to study in Vienna. “I thought: this is not my life, being married and a mother,” she told the Guardian in 2019.

original_article.research:
[Lähde: The Guardian World]
Export’s performances scandalised Austria in the 1960s, but are now recognised for exposing the objectification of the female body

Valie Export, the Austrian performance artist and film-maker who inverted the male gaze in ways that were provocative, shocking and often outrageously fun, has died aged 85.

The artist’s own foundation announced on Thursday evening that Export died in Vienna earlier the same day, three days before her 86th birthday.

She is best known for low-budget performances that scandalised Austria and Germany in the late 1960s, but have since been recognised as milestones in feminist art for exposing the objectification of the female body.

Most notorious was 1968’s Tapp und Tastkino (Tap and Touch Cinema), for which Export strapped a model theatre stage to her chest and invited shoppers in Vienna’s city centre to touch her bare breasts through a tiny curtain. Her artist colleague Peter Weibel rallied passersby through a megaphone, and timed each “action” with a stopwatch.

The zeal with which she laid bare patriarchal power structures was also on display in the centrepiece of her 1980 show at the Venice Biennale. Entitled Geburtenbett (Birth Bed), it showed an outsized female abdomen with crooked legs on a mattress, red neon strip lights streaming from her vulva, and a TV transmitting a Catholic mass where the head would be.

“Valie was one of the most visionary feminist artists to emerge in Europe in the second half of the 20th century,” her gallerist Thaddaeus Ropac said in a statement. “Her passing marks the loss of a singular perspective in contemporary art, one that influenced artists across generations. Her pioneering work continues to be of such great urgency.”

Born Waltraud Lehner in 1940 in Linz, Export boarded at a convent school as a child but left at 14 to study at the city’s School of Arts and Crafts. She married and had a child before she turned 20, but soon after decided to divorce and place her daughter into temporary care with an older sister in order to study in Vienna. “I thought: this is not my life, being married and a mother,” she told the Guardian in 2019.

Custody rights for her daughter were temporarily withdrawn by a judge when she was sentenced on pornography charges in 1970, over her co-editorship of a book on Viennese Actionist art.

payload.title: Feministisen taiteen uranuurtaja Valie Export on kuollut 85-vuotiaana
payload.summary: Itävaltalainen performanssitaiteilija ja elokuvantekijä Valie Export kuoli Wienissä 85-vuotiaana. Hänen 1960-luvulla kohua herättäneitä teoksiaan pidetään nykyisin feministisen taiteen merkkipaaluina.
payload.content:
Itävaltalainen performanssitaiteilija ja elokuvantekijä Valie Export on kuollut 85-vuotiaana Wienissä. Hänen oma säätiönsä kertoi kuolemasta torstai-iltana. Export kuoli aiemmin samana päivänä, kolme päivää ennen 86-vuotissyntymäpäiväänsä. Hänet tunnettiin taiteilijana, joka haastoi mieskatsetta ja naisen kehon esineellistämistä poikkeuksellisen suorasukaisilla teoksilla.

## 1960-luvun kohusta taidehistorian merkkiteoksiin

Valie Export tunnettiin taiteilijana, joka haastoi voimakkaasti käsityksiä naisen kehosta, katseesta ja yhteiskunnallisesta roolista. Hänen 1960-luvun lopun matalan budjetin performanssinsa herättivät aikanaan pahennusta Itävallassa ja Saksassa, mutta myöhemmin niitä on pidetty feministisen taiteen keskeisinä teoksina.

Exportin työt käsittelivät erityisesti naisen ruumiin esineellistämistä ja mieskatseen valtaa. Hän käytti julkista tilaa, omaa kehoaan ja provokaatiota keinona pakottaa katsoja kohtaamaan kysymyksiä, jotka olivat tuolloin taidemaailmassa ja laajemmin yhteiskunnassa usein vaiettuja.

Hänen tunnetuimpiin teoksiinsa kuuluvat performanssit Tapp- und Tastkino ja Aktionshose: Genitalpanik. Lisäksi hän teki kokeellisia elokuvia, kuten Unsichtbare Gegner ja Syntagma. Teokset vaikuttivat erityisesti performanssitaiteen, käsitetaiteen ja feministisen nykytaiteen keskusteluihin.

## Waltraud Lehneristä Valie Exportiksi

Export syntyi Waltraud Lehnerinä Linzissä vuonna 1940. Lapsena hän kävi sisäoppilaitosta luostarikoulussa, mutta lähti 14-vuotiaana opiskelemaan Linzin taide- ja käsityökouluun. Nuorena hän avioitui ja sai lapsen, mutta päätti myöhemmin erota ja jättää tyttärensä väliaikaisesti vanhemman sisarensa hoitoon voidakseen opiskella Wienissä.

Taiteilijanimi Valie Export syntyi 1960-luvulla, ja nimen kirjoitusasu oli hänen säätiönsä mukaan osa omaehtoista identiteetin rakentamista. Nimestä tuli samalla merkki taiteilijasta, joka pyrki irtautumaan hänelle annetuista rooleista ja määrittelemään itsensä uudelleen.

## Vaikutus jatkuu nykytaiteessa

Galleristi Thaddaeus Ropac kuvasi Exportia yhdeksi 1900-luvun jälkipuoliskon visionäärisimmistä eurooppalaisista feministitaiteilijoista. Hänen mukaansa Exportin kuolema merkitsee ainutlaatuisen näkökulman menetystä nykytaiteessa, mutta hänen uraauurtava työnsä vaikuttaa edelleen taiteilijoihin yli sukupolvien.
